note: Expected outcomes are written from the frozen task contract, not recorded from a run. Ownership is an exact literal pathset: a declared path owns itself and nothing else. Owned paths are compared as escaped display text, which is unambiguous and reviewable; the raw byte round-trip is asserted separately by the arbitrary-byte case. Where two spellings of one path are expected to produce the same authority, the digests below are equal on purpose.
platform_restricted_cases: A case may declare a platform restriction. It is reported as skipped with its restriction named on machines it does not apply to, and never dropped from the listing.

cases.description: One file declared, shown, and ended. The shape every other case is a deviation from.
A declared path that exists today as a directory. v1 owns an exact pathset, so a directory declaration has no meaning in it and is refused rather than expanded or silently owned.
A symlink is a path object in its own right. Declaring one owns the link, not what it resolves to - so a symlink pointing at a directory is accepted, because the declaration is about the link.
Declaring a path that does not exist yet - the normal case when the task is about to create it. Scope is a declaration, not an observation.
The same path declared twice is one scope, and its digest equals the single-declaration digest.
'docs' and 'docs/guide.md' are two distinct declarations. Under exact ownership neither implies the other, so neither collapses into the other.
'docs/', './docs' and 'docs//' are three spellings of one path. They collapse to one owned path with one digest.
Every declared name here is a filename, not a pattern: glob characters, pathspec magic, and arguments that look like flags. Nothing expands.
Names containing a space, a tab and a newline. Stored literally, rendered escaped, and the newline does not become a second output row.
'--own ../src/strategy.py' typed from tests/ means the same scope as declaring it from the root, and produces the same digest.
Absolute paths, parent escapes, the repository root, the Git administrative directory, and '..' after a named component. All refused, and none leaves a task behind.
A repository with staged work it did not ask AIQE about. The index is byte-identical across start, status and end.
A repository pointing at commands every way it can - clean filter, fsmonitor, shell aliases, an executable hook. Declaring a task runs none of them.
Two linked worktrees hold two independent tasks. Ending one does not touch the other, and the main worktree has no task at all.
Two real processes racing to start a task in one worktree. One wins, one is refused, and exactly one valid record exists.
A process killed mid-write leaves a temporary file that was never renamed. It is not a task: status says so, and the next start succeeds.
An active record that cannot be read is unknown, not unsupported: status and start exit 2. 'task end' discards it, and that is the documented way out.

An active record written under the superseded schema, where a declared path owned its descendants. Reading it under exact semantics would quietly narrow a live task's authority, so it is refused and left untouched. 'task end' discards it and the user starts again; there is no migration.
A symlink planted where AIQE's private state belongs. AIQE refuses rather than writing through it to somewhere it never promised to write.
An owned path whose bytes are not valid UTF-8, declared through the real entry point with byte-preserving argv. The stored bytes equal the bytes typed.
